title: Trade-In Agreements Policy: Agreements per Customer and per Vehicle
content:
**Clause 1. Number of agreements.** Under **Trade-In Agreements** a customer may hold trade-in agreements on any number of vehicles; there is no per-customer maximum.

**Clause 2. One open agreement per vehicle.** One vehicle, identified by its trade VIN, may have only one agreement that is offered, accepted or picked up at a time. A new offer on the same VIN replaces nothing, and it is issued only when the earlier agreement on that VIN has reached declined, expired, cancelled or settled.

**Clause 3. Basis of the check.** Whether an agreement on the VIN is still open is read from Kestrel's own trade-in agreement records for that VIN (the trade VIN and the agreement status), as they stand before the new offer is issued; it is not taken from the customer's account of it.

## Clause 2 by status of the earlier agreement on the same VIN

| Status of the earlier agreement on the VIN | Does it stand in the way of a new offer on that VIN? |
|---|---|
| Offered | Yes |
| Accepted | Yes |
| Picked up | Yes |
| Declined | No |
| Expired | No |
| Cancelled | No |
| Settled | No |

## Points of judgement

- **Several vehicles.** A customer trading two different vehicles holds two agreements, one per VIN; Clause 1 sets no limit on how many.
- **Same vehicle again.** A second offer on a VIN whose agreement is still accepted is not issued; the new offer would not replace the accepted agreement, which stays as it is.
- **What counts as the same vehicle.** Sameness is decided by the trade VIN, not by the description, the customer or the purchase order.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A customer's earlier agreement on a VIN lapsed and shows expired. A new offer on that VIN may be issued, and it is a separate agreement; the expired one is not revived or replaced.
